title: SRE incident notification scripts and escalation cheat-sheet
content:
Purpose:
This draft is a compact, copy-paste friendly set of scripts, templates, and an internal war-room checklist for incident communications. Designed for fast use by on-call engineers and comms leads during live incidents where speed, clarity, and consistent tone matter.

How to use this file:
- Triage owner picks severity and channel (Slack incident channel + status updates).
- Use the shortest template that conveys accurate scope and ETA; prefer transparency over speculation.
- Mark each posted message with an actor (e.g., "SRE (Anika)") and time.
- After stabilization, convert to a status page timeline entry and attach to incident ticket.

1) Severity quick mapping (for comms tone and cadence)
- Sev-1 (major outage): All customers impacted or critical revenue paths blocked. Post immediately to public status page and send targeted emails to affected accounts within 30 minutes. Twice-hourly public updates until resolved.
- Sev-2 (partial outage / degraded): Notice on status page and targeted comms to customers on impacted routes. Hourly updates recommended.
- Sev-3 (minor degraded or single feature): Internal updates and status page update optional; communicate to customer(s) only if a workaround is not available.

2) Public status page templates (short + expandable)
- Initial (post immediately):
  """
  Summary: We are investigating reports of elevated errors and timeouts for the Redwood Inference API in us-west-2 that may affect text generation requests.
  Impact: Some requests may fail or experience higher latency. Not all customers are affected.
  User action: No action required; we are investigating.
  ETA: Next update in 30 minutes.
  Status: Identified - our SRE team is working on mitigation.
  """

- Update (when have more detail):
  """
  Summary: Root cause: increased memory pressure on a model-serving pool after a failed autoscale action.
  Impact: Requests routed to affected pool may see 5–20% increased error rates.
  Mitigation: Traffic has been rerouted to healthy pools and we are restarting one node (progressing).
  ETA: Service-level mitigation in progress; estimated repair in 45 minutes.
  Status: Mitigating - rolling restart and routing changes underway.
  """

- Resolution (final public note):
  """
  Summary: The issue affecting inference requests in us-west-2 has been resolved.
  Impact: Error rates and latency have returned to normal for affected routes.
  User action: No action required.
  Root cause (brief): Autoscaler misconfiguration allowed an unhealthy node to remain in pool under high load.
  Next steps: We will open a post-incident review and publish a detailed timeline and remediation actions within 3 business days.
  Status: Resolved.
  """

3) Customer-facing email template (targeted accounts)
- Subject: Incident affecting inference requests (us-west-2) — [Status: Mitigating]
- Body (paste-ready):
  """
  Hi <Customer Name>,

  We are writing to let you know we are currently investigating an issue impacting inference requests in the us-west-2 region. Some requests may fail or experience elevated latency. Our SRE team has routed traffic away from the affected pool and is performing rolling restarts; mitigation is in progress.

  What we know now:
  - Scope: <describe if account-specific or region-wide>
  - Impact: <e.g., increased 5–20% error rate for generation requests>
  - ETA for next update: <30 minutes>

  We will follow up with a resolution update and a post-incident summary once the incident is closed. If you are experiencing a production-critical outage, please reply with "SEV-1" in the subject and we will escalate.

  Apologies for the disruption — we are actively working on this.

  — Redwood Inference SRE
  """

4) Short Slack templates (internal channels)
- Incident declared (channel message):
  """
  :rotating_light: INCIDENT | Sev-1 | us-west-2 API failures. Triage owner: Anika. Join #sre-warroom-usw. Initial mitigation: traffic reroute in progress. Public status page notified.
  """

- Request for help (page ops or on-call exec):
  """
  @oncall-platform: need help with kernel-level inspection on node gpu-12-usw. Suspect OOMs during KV cache warmup. Posting logs in the warroom.
  """

5) War-room checklist (first 30 minutes)
- Confirm incident triage: severity, scope, owner, and Slack warroom channel.
- Post initial public status page entry using the template above.
- Collect concrete metrics: error-rate spike window, latency percentiles, affected models/routes, and any recent deploys.
- Identify whether rollback, route swap, or capacity scale is safest first action.
- If rollback or routing is used, pick a single owner to execute and announce completion to warroom.
- Notify Customer Success for any high-touch customers likely impacted.

6) Short technical post-mitigation checklist (next 1–3 hours)
- Verify healthy traffic distribution and absence of cascading errors.
- Run smoke tests across typical customer flows and 2 internal canaries.
- Record timeline events in the incident ticket (time-stamped bullets).
- Draft the resolution status page note and customer emails, but do not send until confirmed stable for 30 minutes.

7) Quick escalation matrix (who to ping)
- SRE on-call (primary): available in channel; immediate action owner.
- SRE engineering lead: Marcus Li — escalate if mitigation needs code changes or rollout.
- Platform infra lead: Dario Mendes — escalate if it's infra-level (autoscaler, node health).
- Customer Success escalation: Sofia Kim — coordinate targeted customer comms.
- CTO/VP Eng: ping if customer SLA impact > 2 hours or executive notification required.

8) Tone best-practices (what to avoid)
- Avoid absolutes when you don’t know: do not say "fixed" until verified.
- Avoid technical jargon in public/customer messages. Keep public messages focused on impact and ETA.
- Own the message: if a mistake was made, state the remediation and next steps transparently.

9) Post-incident follow-up quick guide
- Assign postmortem writer within 24 hours and schedule a 60–90 minute postmortem review within 3–5 business days.
- Public postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause, corrective actions, rollbacks/changes made, and verification plan.
- Communicate remedial timeline to customers if the remediation requires longer work (maintenance window).

10) Copy/Paste snippets (for fast editing)
- Public tiny blurb for social/status aggregator:
  """
  We experienced elevated API errors in us-west-2; mitigation underway. Status page: <link>.
  """

- Internal command to capture minimal debug bundle (example):
  """
  /run capture-debug --nodes=gpu-*-usw --since=15m --output=/tmp/incident-<ts>.tgz
  """

Appendix: Examples of small variations you can use when customizing templates
- If only a single customer account is impacted, change the public status page impact line to: "Single tenant incident; the majority of customers are unaffected. Affected customers have been contacted."
- If a mitigation requires a short maintenance window, include planned time and expected effect: "We will take a rolling restart of 3 nodes at 03:00 UTC; expect up to 2–3 minutes of increased latency per restart."

Notes and TODOs for this draft
- Add standardized subject prefixes for customer emails so CS can automatically filter (e.g., [Redwood Incident: Sev-1]).
- Link to archived postmortems for similar root causes (autoscaler, OOM, routing).
- Create a lightweight status-page checklist UI in Console to reduce manual edits.

Document history:
- Drafted 2024-08-15 by Anika Patel
- Reviewed 2024-11-02 by Marcus Li; added routing templates
- Minor edits 2025-01-12 by Dario Mendes (clarified escalation matrix)

End of document.
